Diagnostics of a geographically weighted regression

Source: R/gwr-diagnostics.R
ef_gwr_diagnostics.Rd

Collects the diagnostics of a fitted GWR model (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md section 7.1) in plain R objects: global fit statistics, the global (OLS) reference, the station table (observed, fitted, residuals, leave-one-out residuals, \(s_{ii}\), local R2, bandwidth, neighbours, condition number, status), the bandwidth profile and a table of the flags.

Usage

ef_gwr_diagnostics(object)

Arguments

object

An earthflux_gwr object from ef_gwr_fit().

Value

A list with:

  • fit: list of fit statistics (n, p, rss, sigma_ml, sigma_edf, enp = tr(S), tr_sts, enp_alt = 2 tr(S) - tr(S'S), edf = n - 2 tr(S) + tr(S'S), aicc, aic, cv, rmse_loo, r2);

  • global_reference: OLS with the same design;

  • stations: the station table (see ef_gwr_fit());

  • profile: the bandwidth profile, or NULL for a bandwidth given by the user;

  • flags: data frame with one row per flag record (code, severity, scope, n_flagged, n_total, description).

Details

The local R2 at station i is that of the local WLS fit, $$R^2_i = 1 - \frac{\sum_j w_{ij} (y_j - x_j^\top\hat\beta_i)^2} {\sum_j w_{ij} (y_j - \bar y_{w,i})^2}, \qquad \bar y_{w,i} = \frac{\sum_j w_{ij} y_j}{\sum_j w_{ij}},$$ identical to summary(lm(y ~ x, weights = w_i))$r.squared (decision GW-13). Other software reports other conventions; GWmodel 2.4-1 Local_R2 uses the global fitted values \(\hat y_j = (Sy)_j\) and the unweighted mean of y.

Verification status

tr(S) in AICc: VERIFICADA as content of Gollini et al. (2015, section 6.1). tr(S'S), 2 tr(S) - tr(S'S), edf, sigma_edf, the local R2 and the condition number: CANDIDATA (original definitions in Fotheringham et al., 2002, and Belsley et al., 1980, not read).

See also

Other spatial regionalization functions: ef_gwr_bandwidth(), ef_gwr_fit(), ef_gwr_predict(), ef_gwr_search(), ef_method_gwr(), ef_method_idw(), ef_method_ols(), ef_method_station(), ef_predict_control(), ef_regionalize(), ef_regionalize_cv(), ef_spatial_folds()

Examples

coords <- cbind(c(0, 10000, 0, 10000, 20000, 30000),
                c(0, 0, 10000, 10000, 0, 30000))
elev <- cbind(elevation = c(100, 300, 500, 200, 800, 1200))
ta <- c(20.0, 18.9, 17.5, 19.6, 15.4, 13.1)
fit <- ef_gwr_fit(ta, elev, coords, bandwidth = 20000,
                  kernel = "gaussian")
d <- ef_gwr_diagnostics(fit)
d$fit$aicc
#> [1] 24.412
d$stations[, c("station_id", "residual", "loo_residual", "s_ii")]
#>   station_id    residual loo_residual      s_ii
#> 1          1 -0.12957310  -0.24821127 0.4779726
#> 2          2  0.08010029   0.10633498 0.2467174
#> 3          3 -0.01165763  -0.01596471 0.2697879
#> 4          4  0.11829798   0.17645165 0.3295729
#> 5          5 -0.12601841  -0.25756623 0.5107340
#> 6          6  0.04086582   0.42300900 0.9033926
